title: How Does Costco Actually Make Money?
description:
Costco sells groceries and TVs at razor-thin margins, but its $5.9 billion in membership fees last year equaled about half of its operating profit.
#costco #costcofinds #business #shorts

Sources: Costco fiscal 2026 results (Sept 24, 2026) via GlobeNewswire/Finviz; Mass Market Retailers (Sept 24, 2026); Costco fiscal 2026 Form 10-K; Costco Q4 FY2026 earnings call (Motley Fool transcript); Zacks/Nasdaq (Sept 25, 2026); Fortune interview with Ron Vachris via CNBC and Fox Business (Jun 24, 2024)
Photos: JeepersMedia (Mike Mozart), basykes, m01229, krossbow, Daquella manera, thekirbster (CC BY 2.0, Flickr)
first_comment: Be honest: is your Costco membership worth it, or do you only go for the hot dog? 🌭

scenes.say: Costco's real profit is your membership card.
scenes.source: Rhetorical reversal, explained in the video: FY2026 membership fees $5,907M vs operating income $11,685M = 50.6% (Costco FY2026 release via GlobeNewswire/Finviz; Mass Market Retailers Sept 24 2026: fees $5.91B, operating income $11.69B). Zacks/Nasdaq Sept 25 2026: FY2025 fees 'about half' of operating income.

scenes.say: The store itself runs on razor thin margins.
scenes.source: Costco FY2026 10-K Item 1: '...operate profitably at significantly lower gross margins (net sales less merchandise costs) than most other retailers.' TheStreet via Yahoo Feb 9 2026 (RetailWire: markups capped at 14% outside brands, 15% store brands); Moneywise (caps around 14% / 15%).

scenes.say: Yet last year it made {$9.2 billion|nine point two billion dollars} in profit.
scenes.source: Costco FY2026 release (52 weeks ended Aug 30 2026): 'Net income for the fiscal year was $9.226 billion' (GlobeNewswire via Finviz); Mass Market Retailers Sept 24 2026: 'increased to $9.23 billion'; 10-K cash flow statement net income $9,226M.

scenes.say: {84 million|Eighty four million} members pay just to get in the door.
scenes.source: Costco FY2026 10-K Item 1 membership table: paid members 84,100 thousand; Q4 FY2026 call (Motley Fool via Webull): '84.1 million total paid members, up 3.8% versus last year'; Zacks/Nasdaq Sept 25 2026 (84.1 million). Fee: 10-K 'Our annual fee for memberships is $65 in the U.S.'; TheStreet via Yahoo ($65 Gold, $130 Executive).

scenes.say: Those fees brought in {$5.9 billion|five point nine billion dollars}.
scenes.source: Costco FY2026 release income statement: membership fees $5,907M (vs $5,323M FY2025) (GlobeNewswire via Finviz); Mass Market Retailers Sept 24 2026: 'membership fees increased to $5.91 billion from $5.32 billion'.

scenes.say: About half of Costco's entire operating profit.
scenes.source: 5,907 / 11,685 = 50.6% (FY2026 membership fees vs operating income, Costco release via Finviz; Mass Market Retailers: fees $5.91B, operating income $11.69B). Zacks/Nasdaq: FY2025 fees ~$5.3B 'about half of the company's $10.4 billion in operating income'.

scenes.say: Costco's CEO said it himself: the most important item we sell is the membership card.

visual.quote: The most important item we sell is the membership card.

scenes.source: Verbatim, Ron Vachris to Fortune (May 2024), reported by Fox Business (Jun 24 2024) and CNBC via NBC Chicago (Jun 24 2024): 'The most important item we sell is the membership card.' Same idea on the Q4 FY2026 call: 'Our membership continues to be the most important item we sell'.

scenes.say: The low prices are just why you renew. And {92%|ninety two percent} do.
scenes.source: Costco FY2026 10-K: 'Our member renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026.' Q4 FY2026 call: 'our U.S. and Canada renewal rate was 92.3%'. Zacks/Nasdaq Sept 25 2026: 92.3%. Narration says 'ninety two percent' for US and Canada members (the video's audience).

scenes.say: So next time you flash that card at the door,
scenes.source: Loop line into the hook ('Costco's real profit is your membership card').
